To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Java software is not significantly different from non-Java software with respect to its quality, that the quality of Java software systems is similar to quality of other software systems, that Java software systems contain a significant number of clones, and that the presence of clones does not significantly affect the quality of the system.

the Java language has been successfully used in medium large systems, and that the quality of Java code, as well as its clone content, are comparable to the quality of code written in C/C++ languages.

1) the quality metrics for Java systems are different from the ones for procedural languages, such as C and C++; 2) clone detection is a valuable technique for Java systems, as for procedural ones, and 3) the clone detection technique can be used to identify parts of a system that are not written in the same style.
In summary, our research is concerned with
software quality assessment and clone detection in Java systems.
the development of techniques for the evaluation of Java software systems.

the following issues: (1) the development of a software quality evaluation tool that is applicable to Java language systems and is based on object oriented metrics, (2) the development of clone detection techniques that are applicable to Java language, and (3) the study of clone occurrence in medium large Java systems and their impact on quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Java systems are more compact than C/C++ systems and have a higher percentage of cloned code.
Java systems are not as good as C++ or COBOL systems.
the quality of Java systems is comparable to the quality of C systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DATRIX suite can be extended to handle Java language systems.
Java systems are more complex than C systems, and Java metrics are more complex than the C metrics.
the Java metrics and clone detection tools are useful and can help to improve quality of software systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
software quality assessment and clone detection are important activities in Java systems.
the DATRIX tm suite, with its extensions to Java systems, can be used for assessing the quality of Java systems.
the quality assessment and clone detection techniques developed for procedural programming languages, such as C, can be extended to Java systems.
